content:
alex: Customer reporting they suddenly lost access to audit exports after turning on our new SSO enforcement. They can list logs but download/export returns 403.
maya: Which entitlement are they on? sounds like read vs export scopes.
alex: They’re on enterprise plan, using Okta SAML. User used to hit /v1/audit/export and get CSV. Now getting HTTP 403 with message: "insufficient_scope: audit:export required".
chris: Ok, likely a scopes mapping issue from SAML assertions -> our org entitlements. Can you paste the raw SAML assertion (redact PII) or the claims we get in auth logs?
alex: Pasted to thread DM. Quick summary: acs:auditor role claim is present but our support console shows no retention/export entitlement flag. Also saw the session has scope [audit:read, audit:search] but missing audit:export.
maya: Two common failure modes: 1) SCIM mapping didn't create the org-level entitlement for export, so even if user has role claim we don't apply export flag; 2) OIDC/OAuth token issued without requested scope (client app misconfigured). For SAML the mapping rule is critical.
jasmin: Repro steps requested from customer - can you ask them to 1) open incognito, 2) re-login to SSO, 3) call the export endpoint with curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o out.csv and paste the token header (we can inspect scopes)?
alex: They did. Here's the token introspect output (sanitized): {
  "active": true,
  "scope": "audit:read audit:search",
  "sub": "user:abc123"
}
chris: That confirms token lacks audit:export. Need to check our auth server logs for the SAML->scope translation. @sre-bot can you pull the last saml mapping run for org org-832?
sre-bot: pulled mapping run id saml-map-2026-03-14-09:12:47 for org-832, rule matched group:auditors -> assigned scopes [audit:read,audit:search]
maya: There we go. Rule didn't include audit:export. Did the auditor group change name recently?
alex: Customer claims they added a new group "exporters" in Okta and added user, but SCIM provisioner hasn't synced that group into Redwood.
jasmin: So user appears in Okta UI but not in our group index -> no mapping applied. That would explain missing entitlement.
chris: Short term: we can grant a temporary manual export entitlement on org via admin console for affected user/org so they can export. Long term: fix SCIM sync and add integration check.
maya: For manual fix I can run: UPDATE org_entitlements SET features = features + ['audit_export'] WHERE org_id = 'org-832' -- but need approval from support for manual DB changes.
alex: I'll open escalation ticket with AB#4519 and tag security for change control. Customer says exports are urgent for compliance audit in 48h.
jasmin: Also need to confirm retention entitlement is set; exports can be blocked if retention policy prohibits exporting older records. Customer asked about retention slices older than 90d.
chris: Good point. Check their retention policy: org-832 retention = 180 days, export_allowed = true currently (per last snapshot) but only for users with audit_export entitlement.
maya: Action items: 1) Grant temporary manual audit_export to org-832 (support request), 2) Trigger SCIM full sync for the customer, 3) Update SAML mapping rule to include audit:export for group auditors or ensure exporters group is mapped, 4) Follow up with customer with repro steps and confirm CSV download works.
alex: I ran the manual entitlement grant (support ticket 4519) and confirmed admin console shows audit_export: true. Customer retried and reports success: "Export started, received CSV", no 403 now. :tada:
jasmin: Log the remediation steps in the customer record and link to KB on SSO->entitlement mapping.
chris: Also add a monitoring alert: if a token introspect returns audit:read without export for >10% of org admins, create a sync job or notify support.
maya: I'll draft the KB and SCIM troubleshooting checklist. Include common curl introspect commands:
```
# get token header
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/oauth/introspect
# expected scope includes audit:export
```
alex: Customer follow-up: they want confirmation this won't recur after they add exporters group. I told them we'll run manual sync and validate mapping rules. They've asked for proof that future role changes auto-provision within 24 hours.
jasmin: Set expectation: SCIM full sync runs every 6 hours by default. We can trigger immediate sync for enterprise customers on request, note in ticket.
alex: Closing notes: Escalation resolved by manual entitlement grant + SCIM sync trigger. Next steps: root cause = missing group in our SCIM mirror and mapping rule missing audit:export; owner: maya for mapping change; owner: eng-infra for SCIM health check. Leaving ticket open until SCIM runs and passes.
support-bot: Incident closed: temp entitlement applied, monitoring rule created, KB draft linked to ticket 4519.
alex: Thanks team. I'll follow up with customer in 1h to confirm they completed their compliance export and attach the CSV delivery confirmation.
